body:
The rationale is inverted, in the comment whose whole job is to stop someone reverting this.

> Widening the array would silently **shorten** every one of those loops.

`COUNT_OF(x)` is `sizeof(x) / sizeof((x)[0])`. Widen the element type to `uint16_t` and `sizeof(array)` goes 4 -> 8 while the element count stays 4, so a `sizeof`-bounded loop runs **eight** iterations over a four-element array. It reads two elements past the end. Widening lengthens the loop into an out-of-bounds read; it cannot shorten it.

The refactor is right and all three sites are right. Just flip the failure mode: "would silently run every one of those loops past the end of the array".

User-facing, and it names a string the app does not show on this card.

> A clone or Write UID reports "not a magic tag" on one.

A gen3 card ignores the gen2 backdoor, so the UID reads back **unchanged**, which is `NotGen2`, not `Fail`. `iso15693_poller.c:1358-1366` reports it and the scene routes to `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_gen1_optin.c`, whose title is **"Not gen2 magic card"** (`:28`) and which offers the destructive gen1 retry.

Your own enum doc has it exactly right at `nfc_magic_app_i.h:107-109`:

> Defensive fallback only: a card that really isn't magic leaves the UID unchanged, which is NotGen2 rather than Fail, and lands on the gen1 opt-in screen instead of here.

Worth adding the omission too, since this bullet is the gen3 hazard note: accepting that opt-in on a gen3 card sends four ordinary WRITE BLOCKs into 56/57/62/63, so the **clone** path can damage a gen3 card, not only the wipe. The bullet currently warns about the wipe alone.

The rest of the bullet checks out - `iso15693_poller.c:1233` really does go straight to the sweep with no backdoor write or magic check, and 0x10/0x11 and 0x14/0x15 are low enough that any sweep reaches them.

This one cost me a false finding, so I want to be precise about it.

> nothing accepted, so the wipe short-circuits to this screen **before any of the truncation reporting**.

I read that, believed it, and worked up a finding that a cut wipe which cleared nothing loses the cut entirely. Then I read four lines further:

```c
if(instance->iso15693_result.pass_truncated) {
    furi_string_printf(text, "No block accepted the\nzero-write.\nTimed out at block %u.", ...
```

It reports it. The routing half is correct - `wiped == 0` gives Fail at `iso15693_poller.c:1252`, `nfc_magic_scene_write.c:490` maps that to NothingWiped, so `WipeStopped` really is unreachable for that card. What you mean is "before the *WipeStopped* truncation reporting". As written it is a claim about the screen it is printed on, and the next sentence in the same comment concedes it ("the cut replaces the prose rather than adding to it").

You wrote the accurate version of this fact 90 lines up at `:181-183`, with no overreach: *"A card that refuses EVERY write never reaches this screen: it clears nothing, so the wipe short-circuits to the nothing-wiped branch below."* That phrasing here too.

Same overreach as `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_write_fail.c:271`, same fix.

> that one clears nothing, so the wipe short-circuits to NothingWiped **before any truncation reporting** -- see the note on that screen.

The note on that screen is `write_fail.c:274-278`, which prints "Timed out at block %u". The claim is "before the *WipeStopped* truncation reporting"; drop the "any".

This re-introduces the round-6 error in the framing sentence directly above its own correction.

> Two different cards **separate them, in opposite directions**, and neither is the other:
>   past the claim -- ... so **`blocks_total == cut_block` exactly**.

The first of the two cards does not separate them at all, and the bullet says so three lines later. Nor can any card separate them in "opposite directions": `blocks_total` is `highest_present + 1` and is structurally `<=` the cut, which `:171` states in the line just above.

What the two cards actually differ in is where the **cut** lands relative to the **advertised count** - which is what the bullets' own labels say ("past the claim" / "below the claim"). That is a different pair of quantities from the one the framing sentence names. Something closer to: "Two cards put the cut on opposite sides of the advertised count, and only one of them opens a gap here."

`:257` then propagates the phrasing: *"see the field's own doc for the two cards that separate them."*

Fails on the one card this whole block is about.

> the WIPE pays more on the same geometry. It runs a card-present inventory every `ISO15693_POLLER_WIPE_ABSENT_RUN` **absences**, and a full re-probe of the trailing run **after the loop**

Both extra costs are driven by absences, and `absent_run` only increments at `:986`, on the read-failure path. The card this bound exists for - refuses every write, answers a read at every address - accumulates **zero** absences, so it pays no inventory and has no trailing run to re-probe. On that geometry the two passes cost the same. The claim holds only when the geometry contains absent blocks, which the sentence does not say.

Two smaller things in the same bullet:
- "after the loop" is misplaced. The radio re-probe is *inside* the loop at `:1036-1056`, fired when a run trips. What runs after the loop (`:1108-1119`) is the tail-drop, which reads the activation cache through `block_held_data` and costs no airtime. `:173-174` already has this right.
- The inventory is also gated on `!claimed_range_attempted` (`:1002`), so it only runs below the advertised count.

Right conclusion, wrong pass credited.

> because **the sweep** reads on every refused block too, not only the empty ones

"Sweep" is this file's word for the wipe, used that way throughout. The wipe has never had an emptiness-conditional read - its read at `:968` is what *determines* emptiness, so "not only the empty ones" is not a property it could ever have had. The pass that changed is the **clone**, and this file documents it at `:702-707`: *"Paid on EVERY persistent failure, not only the empty ones."*

Last round's version of this sentence had it the right way round ("since the probe went onto every persistent failure rather than only the empty ones"). The rewrite moved the attribute from the clone to the wipe.

The arithmetic around it is sound - I checked `write_block_retried` (3 writes, 3 delays, no break before the last one) and `3 * ISO15693_POLLER_VERIFY_RETRY_MS == 15ms`.

Contradicted 11 lines down, by text this round added.

> The clock stopped the sweep with blocks **the card still claims** unattempted.

`:178-181`: *"on a card that accepts some writes and then answers reads everywhere the cut lands above the claim"*. When the cut is above the claim there are no claimed blocks left unattempted - and `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_partial_details.c:107-113` has a whole branch printing *"Every claimed block was attempted."*

The opening sentence describes only the below-the-claim case. It needs the same either-side framing the rest of the comment now has.

The bound is right; the reason given for it is not.

> getting past the claim at all requires never hitting that many consecutive absences, since past the claim such a run ends the sweep.

You can hit 8+ consecutive absences below the claim and still get past it: `claimed_range_attempted` is false there, so the trip falls through to `continue` at `:1001-1009` without ending the sweep, and one later block that answers zeroes the run. That is the floor doing exactly what it is for.

What actually bounds the gap is the run still open **at the cut**: the deadline is checked at the top of the iteration, so `absent_run <= ISO15693_POLLER_WIPE_ABSENT_RUN - 1` at that point on every path, giving `cut_block - blocks_total <= 7`. Same bound, and it survives the floor.

The qualifier list is missing its top entry.

> Show the most significant (real data loss > gen1 UID clobber > AFI/DSFID).
> A cut sweep is not among them: it has its own reason code and screen.

There are four qualifiers, not three: `pass_truncated` (`:242`) > `capacity_confirmed` (`:248`) > `used_gen1` (`:255`) > `identity_failed` (`:258`). The omitted one is **first**, and `:243` says so itself ("Outranks the rest on a cut run").

"A cut sweep is not among them" is defensible if "sweep" is read as wipe-only, since a cut wipe does get `WipeStopped`. But the only cut run that reaches this branch is a cut **clone**, which per `:22-23` has "no reason code of its own" - and the sentence sits directly above the branch that handles it.

Pre-existing text (`9c404bc4`); the qualifier that falsified it landed in `64326417`, so this was mine to catch last round and I did not.

The distances point at the wrong neighbours.

> Two of the clears live inside the densest reasoning in this file, **three and five lines from a set**, where `|=` and `&= ~` differ by two characters

There are exactly two clears (`:1054`, `:1118`) and four sets (`:685`, `:734`, `:977`, `:985`). The nearest set to either clear is `:985` - **69** and **133** lines away. What actually sits 2 and 5 lines from those clears is `clone_failed_count++` (`:1052`, `:1113`), which is not a bitmap op, so the `|=` / `&= ~` hazard the sentence invokes does not apply to them.

"Two of the clears" also implies more than two exist.

The helper is worth having and the underlying point stands - a slip at `:1054` would be `mark_failed` where `unmark_failed` belongs, inside an if/else. Just describe that, rather than a proximity that is not there.

Two live descriptions of `blocks_total` that disagree, and neither is exact.

Here (rewritten this round): *"highest_present + 1 -- a **COUNT of the blocks proven present**, not an index"*.
`nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_partial_details.c:88` (untouched): *"blocks_total is **the highest that answered**"*.

`highest_present + 1` is the size of the range up to the highest proven block, not a count of proven blocks: `wipe_note_present` folds interior absences in, so on a card with a dead stretch that resumes, `blocks_total` exceeds the number actually proven present. And `partial_details.c` describes `highest_present`, which is one less again.

`iso15693_poller.h:171` has the phrasing that survives both: "a COUNT", unqualified. No code is wrong here - the WipeStopped line subtracts `failed` anyway - but three descriptions of one field should not be three different things.

**My error - please revert this to `<`.** The finding I left last round was wrong, and I sent you the wrong way.

`blocks_advertised` is a **count** (`iso15693_poller.c:861`, `iso15693_3_get_block_count`); `cut_block` is an **index**. At equality the claimed blocks are 0..N-1 and the cut sits at index N, which is the first block *past* the claim. So the branch you moved away from was the accurate one:

> "Sweep hit its time limit at block N, past the N this card claims. Every claimed block was attempted; anything above the cut was not."

That is exactly true at equality. The branch it now takes renders "at block N **of the N** this card claims" for an index that is not one of the N, and reads as a completed fraction on the one boundary where the sweep really was cut.

The justification at `:96-98` is mine too, and it is a non-sequitur: "block N itself was not attempted" is equally true of both branches, so it cannot pick between them. Revert the operator and drop those three lines.

Dead conjunct.

```c
if(instance->write_state == Iso15693WriteStateStart &&
   instance->mode != Iso15693PollerModeInfo) {
```

Info mode returns unconditionally six lines up at `:1487-1493`, so `:1499` cannot be reached in Info mode. The `Iso15693PollerEventCardDetected` doc at `iso15693_poller.h:50-51` ("Not sent in Info mode") is already guaranteed by that early return.

`alloc` is a partial copy of the reset list, which is worse than either doing it fully or not at all.

`:1512-1521` sets 10 fields; `iso15693_poller_start_internal:1548-1572` sets 26, including all 10 of those. `running` starts false and every public start entry point routes through `start_internal` (which asserts `!running`), so nothing can read the struct before the full reset. The load-bearing lines here are the three allocations and `running = false`.

The problem is that it reads as *a* reset list while being 16 fields short of the real one - `pass_truncated`, `uid_changed`, `gen1_attempted`, `progress_step` and the rest are absent, and the struct is `malloc`'d, so those are garbage until a start. Anyone adding a field and grepping for where fields get zeroed finds two lists and has to work out which is authoritative.

Either cut `:1512-1521` down to the allocations plus `running = false`, or have it call the same reset `start_internal` uses. One place.

This loop is byte-identical to `:320-323`, and `nfc_magic_scene_write_confirm.c:39-42` is a third copy producing the same output written the other way round (`if(i == 3)` *after* the byte instead of `if(i == 4)` before it).

Two knock-ons from the duplication: the rationale comment ("Two 4-byte groups, unspaced: the spaced form the Info screen uses is 23 characters and overruns the 128px line here") lives only on **this** copy, so a reader arriving at `:320` first gets no explanation; and the third copy has already drifted to the opposite loop shape.

A `nfc_magic_iso15693_uid_cat(FuriString*, const uint8_t*)` next to `nfc_magic_scene_partial_details_common.*` covers all three. `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_info.c:18-20` is the spaced 8-byte form and deliberately stays out of it - which is the distinction the comment here is already drawing.

Small, but it undoes part of the point of hoisting the titles out.

The switch follows the render chain's order for every case except this one: `Partial` is chain position 4 (`:220`) but switch position 11, last before `default`. Everything else lines up. Moving `case ...ReasonPartial` up to sit after `OverCapacity` lets the two lists be read in lockstep, which is what makes "does every branch still have the right title?" a one-pass check.

189 columns. `ColumnLimit` is 99 and `ReflowComments: false`, so `ufbt format` cannot see it - I ran it, it is clean.

This is the comment you rewrote this round, and one of this round's own commits is titled *"a comment line 155 columns wide"*. The new sentence was appended to the existing line rather than reflowed. Break after "not an Exit." and the paragraph is back in the 100-105 band the rest of these files sit at.
110 columns, against 96-104 for the surrounding block. `fdd2a5d3` rewrote the sentence without rewrapping the paragraph. Same class as `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_write_fail.c:403`, much smaller.
